title: HFlowContainer crash
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in 4.5.stable, 4.5.1.stable ### System information Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7283) - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 31.92 GiB memory ### Issue description HFlowContainer can sometimes cause either crash or extremely long lag spike (8-20 seconds). In scenario where it causes long lag spike, UI can end up malformed (elements of HFlowContainer can be overlapping, wrong size). ### Steps to reproduce (With different texts to trigger word wrapping) Either: A) Run the MRP and click the button. This will cause the project to hang for a long time, before finally showing up. B) Before running the MRP, make the ScrollContainer visible in the scene tree. This causes the project to crash on startup. Some notes: This uses a custom font and has slightly complex setup for the elements. It also contains some random text from our game. I believe neither the font nor the exact text matters, but it would require other control sizing property values. My **belief** (no definitive proof, so might red herring) is that there is some sort of infinite loop happening when HFlowContainer is doing layout for its children, when the children have word wrapping, AND somehow this causes an oscillation between "should show scrollbar" and "should not show scrollbar". Some random changes that make the bug go away with the exact setup in the MRP: * Making the vertical scroll either ALWAYS or NEVER enabled. * Changing margins, font sizes, minimum sizes, etc. * Changing the HFlowContainer to be of type GridContainer instead, and setting columns manually. I would also like to note that, even though this MRP is **incredibly** specific in its setup, we have had multiple crashes due to this bug in our actual game project. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [h_flow_crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22936818/h_flow_crash.zip)
